# Native Codex evidence

The behavior reference remains v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Ignored collectors verify imported module bytes against that commit before collecting results. Native maintained tests use saved observations and actual Rust peers; no Python helper, interpreter or compatibility fallback is required by this implementation. The [official app-server documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) describes the JSONL handshake, request correlation and turn completion contract. The original provider checkpoint below used installed Codex 0.158.0; [current-version acceptance](#current-codex-model-metadata) separately renews 0.160.0. Generated version-specific schemas remain scratch evidence.

| Fixture | Independent observations | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `released-codex.json` | 170 catalog rows, 49 alias/default selections, 96 rewrite decisions, exact capability overrides and environment filtering | `4b8ba60238716135f710cb99f90d040b45fc11180ec34b228b49ec9cded6ea6f` |
| `released-codex-wire.json` | 50 real JSONL child-process sessions through the independent native server | `61cf806a5d553adface81a17eca14bf02c62c21b81ab8e5b16496038fb79f062` |
| `released-installed-codex.json` | Two real installed-CLI sessions through a private loopback Responses provider | `75a2b5c35a4f14bbbc264c00ded4508d3614b67ce33507c6820d5e124d7bbdfa` |

The native process comparison checks exact ASCII JSONL frames, request IDs, pagination, explicit and hidden aliases, default selection, current model reporting, images/offsets, effort/tier, partial deltas and completion. Only random workspace and specification paths are normalized. It checks argument overrides, environment names, 0700 workspaces, removal and child reaping. Standard error is discarded even under large diagnostic output. Natural exit/restart preserves request numbering; cancellation cannot restart a client, while `spawn` creates an independent lifecycle. Short request and turn budgets produce the released controlled errors without provider bodies or private paths.

The transport confirms empty environments, ephemeral threads and no instruction sources, disables each inherited MCP server by name, checks its capability inventory and refuses server-initiated requests with JSON-RPC `-32601`. Exposed tools, resources, paginated inventories, model changes, unknown tool items/methods, malformed or oversized deltas and incomplete turns cannot produce replacement text. The peer observes the refusal before completing the pending RPC; shutdown cannot race that observation. Trace lines are encoded and appended in one write so termination cannot create misleading partial evidence.

The process comparison exposed an initial Rust temporary-directory mode of 0755 under the current umask. The production builder now requests 0700 before launching any child. Cleanup drops queued notification content after cancellation and reaps the child before deleting its workspace. Tests additionally exercise a child that ignores SIGTERM and requires the bounded SIGKILL path, missing executables, cancellation during a turn, disabled routes and a compatible route that freezes its alias and ignores Codex-only speed settings. Executable lookup is shared with the already-verified audio services and checks actual access rights, including the system fallback when PATH is absent.

Global instruction files are masked with actual bubblewrap mounts in a private child namespace; the parent files are unchanged. The installed-CLI check uses isolated HOME/CODEX_HOME, disables remote catalogs and WebSockets, supplies only synthetic input to loopback HTTP and never reads a real credential or invokes remote inference. Every captured model request has an empty tool catalog; canary MCP and command markers remain absent, and private instruction canaries never enter the requests.

Codex 0.158.0 refuses an unsolicited backend `exec_command` internally and makes a second model request without exposing an operation item to Mluva. Both the unchanged release and native client accept the subsequent successful text result. The fixture records this actual behavior; it does not assert that Mluva received or rejected an event the CLI never exposed. The legacy smoke script also accepts successful text, or a controlled refusal if an operation is exposed; its actual isolated baseline passes. Direct exposed-operation refusals remain covered by the 50 process cases.

The shared factory snapshots settings, routes disabled/compatible/Codex requests, preserves short catalog/title budgets and uses the released 40,000-character document rewrite bound. Codex's standalone transform default remains 8,000. A 9,000-character factory rewrite is independently compared with the release so document support cannot accidentally inherit the smaller bound. Frozen rewrite cases also preserve separate unsupported-speed and unsupported-thinking errors: the released controller gives the former an actionable message and handles the latter through its generic failure path. Native controllers can preserve that behavior without matching error text.

Five ordinary native Codex tests pass. The installed-CLI test is ignored by default because it requires the pinned CLI and working bubblewrap; it was explicitly run successfully after review:

`make linux-codex-isolation-test` now runs that existing native installed-CLI owner in private HOME/XDG, network/PID namespaces and devices, with inherited credentials and desktop/bus environment removed. Both actual loopback sessions pass with Python and uv blocked by positively exercised traps. The obsolete 164-line Python checker is removed; its baseline also passes. No Rust cases, fixture bytes or production behavior change. The runner keeps its receipt under `tmp/codex-isolation/` and does not perform remote inference or account verification.

The five ordinary Codex siblings and remaining 571 Python tests pass, plus Ruff/formatting for 148 files, changed-shell ShellCheck/syntax and diff checks. The installed-CLI fixture remains byte-identical at the hash above. The prior full native/Clippy/format/generated gate remains applicable because this cutover changes no Rust/Cargo/fixture inputs. Raw checks are `tmp/native-codex-cutover-baseline-python.log`, `tmp/native-codex-cutover-traps.log`, `tmp/native-codex-cutover-siblings.log` and `tmp/native-codex-cutover-python.log`. Final preservation review was performed sequentially in this session.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p mluva-providers --test codex installed_codex -- --ignored
```

The ordinary workspace passes 95 tests, with three private GTK tests and this CLI test excluded from the default run. The three GTK tests retain their earlier explicitly executed evidence and were not rerun for this provider change. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass. Real account entitlement/inference, keyring integration, managed local CPU/GPU models, complete application controllers and workflows, distribution, final Python removal and performance measurements remain pending. The installed app/widget remain 1.6.0. All synthetic peer binaries must be excluded from installation.

## Current Codex model metadata

5 October 2026: unchanged v1.6.0 source is independently exercised against the actual installed `codex-cli 0.160.0` ELF. All 91 released source/resource inputs are verified before collection and again at final review. The six cases cover explicit text, an unsolicited backend command, the eleven-model catalog/default, automatic model selection, explicit-model screenshots with effort/tier and automatic-model screenshots. Full rewrite input/image bytes, capture offset, catalog rows, model identifiers, effort/tier, output and deltas are preserved. The separate `released-installed-codex-0160.json` is 7,923 bytes, SHA-256 `0ca392f0251d931bd051757fb22a5de66bc5a7eb85134a965434e4c80c2a4618`; the earlier 0.158.0 fixture stays byte-identical. Explicit legacy model requests establish the transport contract, not account entitlement or availability.

The released feature overrides do not fully remove capabilities selected by newer model metadata. Its automatic-model requests omit the top-level tool catalog but expose nine operations in inline namespaces. A genuine native negative detects those operations. An external provider profile changes only `tool_mode`, `multi_agent_version` and `experimental_supported_tools`; unchanged released application code then produces the same six outputs and request settings with both tool surfaces empty. A second genuine negative enables inherited feature flags and detects tools surviving that intermediate repair. Neither unsafe source behavior nor failing native output is accepted as the desired permission contract.

Native CLI startup now dumps the selected CLI's catalog in the existing owned RAM workspace, preserves its metadata apart from those three capability fields, and passes the private 0600 profile back to app-server. It also explicitly disables `code_mode_only`, `current_time_reminder`, `send_message_to_user_async` and `deferred_executor`; the original permission policy and JSONL frames remain unchanged. Both startup children share instruction masking, allowed environment, parent-death guards and cleanup. Snapshot output is bounded to 4 MiB and the existing request timeout; invalid/oversized catalogs, externally held cancellation and an actual timeout each return a controlled path-free error, remove the workspace, reap the child and never start the server. Custom JSONL transports without an `app-server` subcommand retain their existing contract. The extra CLI startup work is bounded; no startup-speed improvement is claimed.

The existing native installed-CLI owner passes all six current cases and both old 0.158.0 cases with adversarial user feature flags and a canary MCP server. Top-level and inline capabilities are empty; MCP/command markers and instruction disclosure are absent. The current owner is also run with positively exercised absolute `/usr/bin/python`, `/usr/bin/python3` and `/usr/bin/uv` traps, including its children; none is invoked during acceptance. Fifty frozen JSONL sessions and four new snapshot fault scenarios pass through existing owners. No new test, ignored owner, binary, dependency or production test seam is added, and no full SDK catalog is maintained or shipped.

Actual `make linux-test` passes 142 tests, zero failures and 71 ignored checks across 98 suites, both strict Clippy variants, formatting and generated consistency. The final rebuilt production bundle and separately rebuilt isolated GTK process owner pass in 179.65 seconds: four Live flows/27 states plus seven-state crash reopening, three preview flows/10 states, earlier 38 bootstrap states/13 actions/five CLI contracts, cold recording/quit and three startup faults. Final full-window RGB, distinct History/audio owners and fresh-owned reply match the earlier immutable observations, including the already documented explicit crash-cleanup improvement. The [compact current report](../../../../docs/verification/rust-worker-lifecycle/current-codex.json) retains identities, raw HTTP receipts, genuine negatives and final package/native evidence. Temporary original-language collectors, SDK source/catalogs and binaries remain ignored scratch. The subsequent [assembled actual-SDK Live comparison](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/bootstrap-managed-live-evidence.md#assembled-live-with-the-actual-current-sdk) adds fifteen states/ten requests to the existing process owner and reruns both real SDK component versions after sharing their response encoder. Account/inference, broader actual-SDK controllers/images/settings, wider providers/interleavings and physical/Wayland/platform acceptance remain open. Published/installed 2.0.0 and complete-workflow matrix statuses are unchanged.
